rationale: The route (CONVERSATION_MEMBERSHIP→CONVERSATION→MESSAGE→REACTION→USER→WORKSPACE_MEMBERSHIP) is fully exercised: the prompt asks for channel members gated on an admin's eyes-reaction to a specific OOM message, and the base seed already contains the anchor message (1706110000.000100 in C03IJKL9012) and its only reaction (bot U01AGENBOT9, eyes), whose workspace role is 'member' per user_teams — correctly making 'absent' the justified resolution mode. The planned additions (admin reacting with eyes to the wrong message, admin reacting with wrong emoji to the right message) are legitimate design-stage placeholders per the stated allowance for compiler-created rows, and they don't disturb the uniqueness of the failing chain since they target different messages/emojis. Candidate membership rows for #engineering are correctly marked negative since they can never be surfaced. Written attributes (channel_members.channel_id/user_id/joined_at) are bare columns, access_plan uses only documented APIs (search.messages, reactions.get, users.info, conversations.members) consistent with runtime_qualifications, and the workspace-role vs conversation-role distinction is correctly maintained (channel_members has no role field). The prompt is concise and realistic, and the absence is non-trivial, requiring the solver to trace reactor role rather than assume any eyes-reactor suffices.
